## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 57, titled *Nahāna* ("Bathing too often"), is an expiation rule within the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic bathing habits [SuttaCentral]. Under this rule, a monk residing in the central Ganges plain who bathes more than once a fortnight—except under prescribed exceptions such as being dirty or unwell—commits an offense that must be confessed [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary literature passages in the dossier directly examine this text; rather, they refer to the distinct rule Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 57 or constitute unrelated non-Buddhist citations.

SuttaCentral identifies full parallels across the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-pc57*), the *Parivāra*, and the monastic codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Upāliparipṛcchā traditions preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. It also lists corresponding rules for nuns, including Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 138 [SuttaCentral].
